title: Microscopes in medicine
examples: What is the difference between a microscope and a magnifying glass?
How much can a microscope actually make things look bigger?
What do doctors look at when they use a microscope?

explain.say: A microscope helps us see things too small for our eyes.
We use microscopes to look at tiny living things called cells.
Doctors use them to view germs, which are very tiny living organisms.
Magnification means making something look much larger than it really is.
To look at a sample, we place it carefully on a glass slide.
In everyday life, you see this when a dentist checks your teeth.

faq.q: What is the difference between a microscope and a magnifying glass?
faq.a: A magnifying glass only makes things look bigger up close. A microscope uses lenses and mechanisms to achieve much higher magnification levels.
asks: Can a magnifying glass see cells?
What is the main difference between these tools?

faq.q: Are all germs dangerous to humans?
faq.a: No, many germs are harmless and are actually part of our normal body bacteria. Some are helpful while others can make us sick.
asks: Are some germs good for us?

faq.q: How do I prepare a sample for the microscope?
faq.a: You must place the sample onto a clean glass slide and often cover it with a thin glass piece called a coverslip. This keeps it flat.
asks: What do I put on the slide?

faq.q: What does the magnification setting do?
faq.a: The magnification setting changes how many times bigger the image appears to you. You change it to see different levels of detail.
asks: How do I change the zoom?

faq.a: A cell is the basic, smallest unit of life that makes up all living things. Everything alive is made up of one or more cells.
asks: Is a cell the smallest thing?

facts: Cells are the fundamental building blocks of all known living organisms.
Microscopes allow us to view structures too small to be seen with the naked eye.
A slide is a thin, flat piece of glass used to hold the specimen.
Magnification power is calculated by multiplying the eyepiece power by the objective lens power.

quiz.say: If a microscope has an eyepiece of ten times and an objective lens of forty times, what is the total magnification?
quiz.why: You multiply the two lens powers together to find the total magnification.

wrong.1: Adding the numbers is incorrect because magnification requires multiplication.
wrong.2: You should only multiply the eyepiece by the objective lens, not by itself.
wrong.3: Dividing the numbers is wrong because the total power increases, it does not decrease.

quiz.say: What is the primary purpose of using a glass slide in microscopy?

options.show: To make the sample look bigger.
options.say: To make the sample look bigger.

options.show: To collect the germs from the air.
options.say: To collect the germs from the air.

options.show: To provide a flat surface for the specimen.
options.say: To provide a flat surface for the specimen.

quiz.why: The slide keeps the sample stable and flat so the light can pass through it correctly.

wrong.0: The slide itself does not provide magnification; the lenses do.
wrong.1: While some stains are used, the slide's main job is physical support, not sterilization.
wrong.2: A slide is for holding a prepared sample, not for passive air collection.

quiz.say: When looking at cells, what structure is responsible for controlling what enters and leaves the cell?
quiz.why: The cell membrane acts like a gatekeeper, controlling the passage of substances in and out.

wrong.0: This is part of the microscope, not a part of the cell itself.
wrong.2: The nucleus controls cell activities, but the membrane controls entry and exit.
wrong.3: The cytoplasm is the jelly-like substance filling the cell, not the barrier.
